cases.name: 01-pdf-ali
cases.content:
Databricks just acquired Tabular, the company behind Apache Iceberg. This move highlights a clear trend in our industry: the most effective technology wins when it remains open. We believe that an open-source approach to data infrastructure provides the best path for innovation and long-term utility for our users.

This acquisition brings together the teams behind Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg under one roof. When you look at the technical history of these two projects, it is evident that both have been fundamental to how companies store and process massive amounts of information. By uniting the core contributors of both communities, we are aiming to create better outcomes for every organization managing complex data environments.

The strategic implication here is that we are doubling down on open standards. By removing friction between formats and simplifying how teams work with their data, we allow the market to focus on building rather than navigating proprietary lock-in. This is how we move the entire ecosystem forward. We are looking forward to seeing how these teams collaborate to solve the next generation of data challenges using open and extensible architecture.

cases.name: 02-pdf-matei
cases.content:
The AI industry is moving beyond the era of simply scaling up monolithic models. We see the next wave of progress coming from how we orchestrate multiple models, retrieval, and tools as compound AI systems.

---

This architectural shift is why we are focused on Mosaic and our ML platform. It is not about making one single model bigger; it is about providing the infrastructure to compose these elements into a reliable, coherent system.

---

Building compound AI systems requires a platform that handles the complexity of managing models, data, and tools together. This is where we are directing our efforts to help teams move from experimentation to production.

cases.name: 01-pdf-ali
cases.content:
We recently acquired Tabular, the team behind Apache Iceberg. Bringing the teams behind Spark and Iceberg together under one roof marks a significant moment for the industry and confirms that the best technology wins when it remains open.

Open source is the bedrock of modern data infrastructure. When formats and engines remain accessible, the entire ecosystem benefits from wider adoption and shared innovation. By uniting the core contributors of these two projects, we are doubling down on our commitment to an open approach.

The value of this combination rests on the principle that data platforms should prioritize interoperability over closed, proprietary silos. Customers gain the most flexibility when they have the freedom to choose their tools without being locked into a single vendor's specific architecture. 

This move reinforces that open-source standards are not just an alternative to proprietary solutions, but the primary driver of development in data engineering. We believe that when great minds collaborate on open foundations, the resulting progress helps every organization manage its data more effectively. Our focus remains on supporting these communities as they continue to evolve and scale.

cases.name: 01-pdf-ali
cases.content:
Data infrastructure often stalls when technical standards remain fragmented. Choosing between different ways to structure data creates friction for engineering teams and slows down the adoption of analytics tools. We have always maintained that the best technology wins when it is open, and today we are acting on that belief.

Databricks has acquired Tabular, the company behind Apache Iceberg. This acquisition brings the contributors behind Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg under one roof. By uniting these communities, we are betting on the idea that open-source innovation is the most effective way to build durable data infrastructure.

This move validates the open-source approach to data. When technologies are open, developers can build on standards rather than being locked into vendor-specific silos. Bringing these experts together allows us to collaborate on the evolution of these formats. We believe this supports an accessible ecosystem where the best tools emerge from a collaborative environment. We look forward to working with the community to build a more unified future for data management.

---

At Databricks, we are focused on our ML platform and Mosaic to support this orchestration, providing the tools teams need to develop, monitor, and scale compound AI systems.
